info.title: Three.js voxel Japanese garden with day-night cycle

Build a 3D voxel Japanese garden in Three.js: a pagoda, cherry blossom trees, a koi pond with koi swimming on curved paths, and falling petal particles. Add a day/night cycle with a time slider and lighting that changes smoothly. The camera slowly orbits by default, and the user can drag to orbit."

Design decisions: - Use OrbitControls with autoRotate for default orbit; disable autoRotate when user drags (or keep both: camera target slowly orbits scene center, user can drag) - Actually "camera slowly orbits by default, and the user can drag to orbit" - I'll use OrbitControls with autoRotate enabled by default, and set a flag so that when user interacts, autoRotate pauses temporarily but can resume. Voxel pagoda: - Base platform - Multiple tiers with eaved roofs (boxes stacked with decreasing width) - A spire on top Cherry blossom trees: - Trunk (voxel column) - Canopy (pink voxels in a spherical/cloud shape) Koi pond: - Blue water plane/voxel basin - Koi fish as small elongated boxes or custom geometry swimming on figure-8 or circular paths with sine wave bobbing Petal particles: - Points mesh with pink/white particles, falling with drift, resetting when they hit ground Lighting: - Directional light (sun) moving in arc across sky - Ambient light intensity/color changes day↔night - Hemisphere light for sky/ground - Fog color changes - Maybe a moon at night Time slider: input type=range 0-24, displays current time. Auto-advance in attract mode. Let me write the code now. I'll make it a single HTML file. Structure: ```html Voxel Zen Garden
...
``` Let me now write the full implementation carefully. Voxel helper: function to add a voxel at (x,y,z) with color. Use a shared geometry and instanced meshes per color group? Simpler: create meshes with BoxGeometry and merge via BufferGeometryUtils, or just create many meshes — garden is small, fine. But for performance, use InstancedMesh per material color. Simpler approach: a `scene.addVoxel(x, y, z, colorHex)` that creates a mesh with BoxGeometry(1,1,1), positioned at integer coords + 0.5 center. For a small garden, a few hundred meshes is fine. Actually let's use a single merged geometry for opaque voxels and separate for transparent. Or just use InstancedMesh with one color per batch. To keep code simple and self-contained, I'll create a helper `addVoxel(x,y,z,color)` returning mesh, grouped into a `garden` Group. Maybe a few hundred meshes is OK for a demo. Koi: create a fish shape from a stretched box (Scale 0.3, 0.8, 0.2) with orange/white/black colors, multiple fish. Each fish swims along a path: center point + radius*cos/sin over time, plus sine bobbing. Orient fish toward velocity. Petals: Points or Sprite-like small quads. Use THREE.Points with a BufferGeometry of N particles, each with position, velocity, drift. In update, move down + drift, reset when below ground. Color pink/white. Day/night: - timeOfDay 0-24 hours - sun angle = (timeOfDay / 24) * 2π - π/2 maybe, so at time 6 sunrise, 12 noon, 18 sunset - sun position: x = cos(angle)*radius, y = sin(angle)*radius (positive y up during day) - At night y negative (below horizon), directional light still casts faint moonlight - Ambient light: day 0.6 white, night 0.15 blue-ish - Hemisphere light: sky color day light blue, ground greenish; night dark blue / dark green - Fog: day light blue, night dark blue - Window/warm glow in pagoda at night? Could add point lights in pagoda that turn on at night. Slider: input range min 0 max 24 step 0.1, value linked to timeOfDay. Auto-advance time at rate (e.g., 0.5 hours per second → full cycle in 48 seconds). Pause auto-advance when user drags slider? Maybe keep simple: slider sets time; auto-advance continues but slider moves too. I'll make auto-advance the default (attract mode), slider can override; if user interacts with slider, pause auto for a few seconds? Keep it simple: auto time advances; slider reflects and can set time (setting time while auto advances will be overridden next frame — acceptable but jarring). Better: have `timePaused` flag; slider mousedown pauses auto, mouseup resumes? Let me implement: `let autoTime = true; let timeOfDay = 10;` slider input sets timeOfDay and sets autoTime=false for a while via timeout, then resumes. Simpler: checkbox? No, keep UI minimal: slider + auto checkbox maybe. I'll do: slider controls time; an "auto" toggle button. Attract mode = auto on by default. Also camera auto-orbit: OrbitControls autoRotate = true, autoRotateSpeed = 0.5. When user drags (controls.start), set autoRotate false; on end, maybe re-enable after a timeout? Requirement: camera slowly orbits by default, user can drag to orbit. I'll keep autoRotate always on but user can still drag (OrbitControls allows dragging even with autoRotate; autoRotate continues to rotate around target). Actually with autoRotate enabled, user drag still works but camera keeps drifting. That's fine — "slowly orbits by default, and user can drag to orbit" both satisfied. I'll set autoRotateSpeed slow. Pagoda design: - Base platform: 10x10 stone voxels at y=0..1 - Pillar columns at corners - Tier 1: 8x8 floor, roof extending to 10x10 eaves - Tier 2: 6x6, roof to 8x8 - Tier 3: 4x4, roof to 6x6 - Spire on top Each roof layer: box at center wider than floor below, thin height. Voxel style: build roofs from voxels at corners/edges. Simpler voxel pagoda: For each tier i (0..2): - floor at height h = 2 + i*3, size s = 10 - 2*i, fill with voxels - roof at h+1..h+2, size s+2 overhang, then smaller roof above... Let me do a stylized approach: - stone base: y=0, 12x12 filled - For tier in 0..2: - pillars: 4 corner columns from base up to tier floor - floor: voxels at tier height, size decreasing - roof: a box (voxel shell) at tier height+1, size tier size+2 overhang - top spire: thin column + golden ball To keep code compact, I'll write loops adding voxels. Cherry tree: trunk 2x2 column up to height 6-8, canopy: pink voxels in sphere radius 3-4 around top, with some darker pink/white variation. Koi pond: basin 10x10 at y=0 with water voxels (transparent blue) or just a blue plane. Koi swim above/within. Koi as meshes grouped, animated. Pond edge: stone/rock voxels around. Ground: grass voxels covering area, dirt path, stone lanterns, maybe a bridge over pond. Let me estimate code size — it'll be a few hundred lines. Fine for a single file. Let me write it. Lighting smoothness: lerp colors/intensities each frame toward targets based on timeOfDay. Sun/moon: add a small sphere mesh following sun position, emissive. Skybox: none (fog covers), or a simple gradient via fog only. Fog keeps it simple. Code: ```javascript const scene = new THREE.Scene(); const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(60, innerWidth/innerHeight, 0.1, 100); const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({antialias: true}); renderer.setSize(innerWidth, innerHeight); renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2)); document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement); const controls = new OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement); controls.enableDamping = true; controls.autoRotate = true; controls.autoRotateSpeed = 0.4; controls.minDistance = 8; maxDistance 40; // lights const ambient = new THREE.AmbientLight(0xffffff, 0.6); scene.add(ambient); const hemi = new THREE.HemisphereLight(0x87ceeb, 0x222233, 0.6); scene.add(hemi); const sun = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 1.2); sun.position.set(10, 15, 5); sun.castShadow = true; scene.add(sun); ``` Voxel helper: ```javascript const voxelGeo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1,1,1); function addVoxel(x,y,z,color,parent=scene){ const m = new THREE.Mesh(voxelGeo, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({color})); m.position.set(x+0.5, y+0.5, z+0.5); parent.add(m); return m; } ``` Using MeshStandardMaterial per voxel creates many materials; better use one material and set color per mesh via vertex colors or just create material per unique color (few colors: grass green, stone grey, pink, wood brown, water blue, orange, gold). I'll cache materials by hex. Actually simplest robust: `const matCache = {}; getMat(hex)`. Shadows: enable renderer.shadowMap.enabled, sun.castShadow, voxels receive/cast. Fine. Garden build: Ground plane grass: 20x20 at y=0. Voxels for each cell? 400 meshes — okay-ish but heavy. Better: one big box for grass ground, and voxels for features. But "voxel garden" aesthetic — ground can be a flat box with grass color; features are voxels. I'll do ground as voxel layer? To keep performance fine, ground as single BoxGeometry plane (20x20, 0.1 height) — looks less voxel but acceptable. Actually let me make ground from voxels but only 20x20 = 400 meshes... Each mesh with BoxGeometry — at 60fps fine for desktop. But draw calls 400+ could be okay. Alternatively use InstancedMesh for ground grass. Let me use InstancedMesh for the ground layer to be safe. Simplify: ground = single flat box (not voxel) + features as voxels. The requirement is "3D voxel Japanese garden" — the key structures are voxels. Ground plane fine. Pagoda function: ```javascript function buildPagoda(x,y,z){ const g = new THREE.Group(); // base platform for(dx=-5;dx<=5;dx++) for(dz=-5;dz<=5;dz++) addVoxel(x+dx, y, z+dz, 0x888888, g); // tier floors + roofs let h = 1; for(const [size, over] of [[10,12],[8,10],[6,8],[4,6]]){ // floor for(dx...size) for(dz...) addVoxel at y=h h++; // pillars at corners up to next floor? // roof layer: box overhang over+2 at y=h..h+1 h += 2; } } ``` This is getting complex; let me just write concrete voxel placements with loops in the final file. I'll iterate sizes [12,10,8,6] for roofs, floors [10,8,6,4]. Simpler pagoda: - base stone platform 12x12 at y=0 (y=0 voxels) - tier floor 1: 10x10 at y=1; pillars at four corners from y=0 to y=1 already covered by base... columns at corners rising to each tier. - roof 1: at y=2, size 12x12 (overhang), y=2..3 - floor 2: 8x8 at y=4; roof 2 at y=5 size 10x10 - floor 3: 6x6 at y=7; roof 3 at y=8 size 8x8 - floor 4: 4x4 at y=10; roof 4 at y=11 size 6x6 - spire: 1x1 column y=12..14 at center, top pyramid/ball y=14..15, gold color. Wood color for floors/roofs (0x8b5a2b), stone for base (0x9a9a9a), spire gold (0xd4af37). Add slightly darker roof underside? Skip. Cherry tree: ```javascript function buildTree(x,y,z){ trunk height 7, 2x2 wood voxels canopy center at y+6: sphere radius 3.5, place pink voxels where distance < 3.5 with some randomness, colors pink #ffb6c1 / #ffc0cb / white } ``` Many voxels per tree (~150), 3-4 trees → fine. Koi pond: - basin: hole filled with water — just a blue transparent plane at y=0.1, 10x10, surrounded by stone edge voxels. - Koi: group of fish meshes. Fish geometry: box 0.2x0.4x1 stretched, color orange #ffaa00 with white/black details maybe just orange. Each fish: path center, radius, speed, phase. Position: center + radius*(cos t, 0, sin t) + bob (0, sin(t*2)*0.2, 0). Look at next position. Petals: - 120 particles, positions random in garden area y 8-15, velocity y = -0.05..-0.15, x drift sine. Colors pink/white. Points mesh. Update loop: - timeOfDay += delta * rate (if auto) - update lights: angle = (timeOfDay/24 - 0.25) * 2π → at 6am angle 0 (sunrise at east?), let's define angle = (timeOfDay/24)*2π; sun dir: x=cos(angle)*15, y=sin(angle)*15... At time 6: angle=π/2 → sun at top (noon?) Let's set: time 6 = sunrise. angle = (timeOfDay - 6)/24 * 2π. At time 6: angle 0 → sun at (15, 0)? Hmm want sunrise low on horizon. Define phase = (timeOfDay / 24) * 2π. Sun position: x = cos(phase) * R, y = sin(phase) * R. At phase 0 (midnight?): sun at (R, 0) — not great. Better: angle = (timeOfDay/24) * 2π - Math.PI/2. At time 0: angle=-π/2 → sun at (0,-R) below horizon (night). Time 6: angle=0 → (R, 0) east horizon sunrise. Time 12: angle=π/2 → (0,R) noon overhead. Time 18: angle=π → (-R,0) west sunset. Time 24: back to below. Light color: lerp between night (dark blue ambient 0x202040, intensity 0.2) and day (white, 0.8) based on sun height factor = clamp(sin(phase+...) hmm. Use `dayFactor = Math.max(0, Math.sin(phase))` where phase as above: at time 6 sin(0)=0 → night; time 12 sin(π/2)=1 → day; time 18 sin(π)=0. Smooth. But sunrise/sunset have twilight — use `twilight = Math.max(0, Math.sin(phase + 0.5))` for softer. Keep simple: dayFactor = clamp(sin(phase),0,1); nightFactor = 1-dayFactor. Ambient: color lerp 0x222244 → 0xffffff, intensity 0.2→0.7. Hemi: sky 0x001133→0x87ceeb, ground 0x111122→0x445544. Sun intensity: 0→1.5 (when below horizon, still 0.2 moonlight). Sun position y = sin(phase)*R — negative at night, light comes from below ground but shadow/fog looks okay; also clamp sun position to not go too far below? Directional light position doesn't matter much, only direction. Fine. Fog color: lerp 0x050510 → 0x87ceeb; fog density constant. Sun disk mesh: small sphere at sun position when above horizon, emissive orange/yellow; moon at night: grey sphere below horizon — hide or show faintly. I'll show a "sun/moon" sprite: sphere emissive, visible always at sun position, color yellow day / white dim night. Pagoda interior lights at night: point lights that turn on when nightFactor high. Add 2-3 point lights inside pagoda at height tiers, intensity = nightFactor * 1. Slider UI: ```html
Voxel Zen Garden
Time: 12:00
Drag to orbit • Auto day/night cycle
``` CSS: fixed position, semi-transparent dark bg, white text. JS UI: - slider input: timeOfDay = value; update time display; `autoPaused = true; clearTimeout(resumeTimer); resumeTimer = setTimeout(()=>autoPaused=false, 3000);` — so user interaction pauses auto for 3s then resumes (attract mode returns). Good for kiosk/attract mode. Time display: hour = Math.floor(timeOfDay), min = Math.round((timeOfDay%1)*60), format HH:MM. Camera: start position (15, 12, 15) looking at center. Orbit center maybe (0, 3, 0). controls.target = (0,3,0). autoRotate rotates around target. Koi animation details: - fishCount = 6 - each: center offset (random around pond), radius 1.5-3, speed 0.5-1.2, phase random, bobbing. - position: cx + r*cos(t), waterLevel + sin(t*3+bobPhase)*0.15, cz + r*sin(t) - orientation: compute next pos, lookAt, plus roll. Fish mesh: elongated box: scale(0.15, 0.15, 1). Color orange. Add eye? Skip. Tail wiggle: scale z? Mesh.scale.y = 1 + sin(t*10)*0.1. Nice touch. Petals: - count 100, geometry BufferAttribute position (3N), colors. - each: x,z random in [-15,15], y random 6..16; fall speed; drift speed/direction. - update: y -= fall; x += Math.sin(time+drift)*driftSpeed; if y < 0.5: reset y = 16 (or pond y). Color random pink shades. - Use Points with PointsMaterial (size 0.12, vertexColors true, transparent). Rendering loop with requestAnimationFrame, clock delta. Shadows: renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true; sun.castShadow; set shadow camera bounds. Voxels cast/receive shadow. Ground plane receives. Resizing: handle window resize. Let me also add a stone lantern near pagoda and a bridge across pond? Keep scope manageable: pagoda, 3 trees, pond with koi, petals, ground, path. Maybe a simple stone lantern as voxels. Nice-to-have; include a small lantern function. Path: dirt-colored voxels line from front to pagoda. Optional. I'll add a simple path of 0.5-height? Voxels are full height. Path as row of voxels at y=0... they'd be 1 tall steps — looks like a raised walkway. Fine, "stepping stone path". Or make path flat using thin boxes scaled y=0.1 — non-voxel. I'll add stepping stones: single voxels spaced apart. Let me now also consider: "start an automatic demo or attract mode without any user input" — auto orbit + auto time cycle + animated koi/petals covers this. Write the file now. I'll be careful with the importmap and addons URL. Use unpkg three@0.160.0. Also add `pointer-events` handling: OrbitControls needs click on canvas; UI overlay should not block canvas. Position UI top-left with pointer-events: none except slider. Add `style="pointer-events:none"` on container, slider pointer-events auto. FPS: use requestAnimationFrame. Now, writing all voxel placements: helper `vox(x,y,z,c)` adds to garden group. Materials cached. One concern: many MeshStandardMaterial instances — cache by hex string. Let me write ground: grass plane BoxGeometry(26, 0.4, 26) at y=-0.2? Or voxel ground via InstancedMesh 26x26 at y=0 → 676 instances, one draw call. I'll do InstancedMesh for ground grass voxels at y=0 (each 1x1x1). Then features on top. Also stone edge of pond etc. Actually ground at y=0 voxels means pond water sits inside. Fine: dig out pond area: don't place grass voxels in pond rectangle; place water plane at y=0 there... simpler: place grass everywhere, then pond as blue box (transparent) from y=-0.1 to 0.1 over pond area, stone border voxels around at y=0. Water surface plane at y=0.05. Koi swim at y around 0..0.5 above/below water surface — they'll appear in water. Okay, writing code now. I'll produce one big file. Let me carefully draft. ```html Voxel Zen Garden
VOXEL ZEN GARDEN
12:00
